verdict.summary: A multi-tenant advertising agent needs a Business app, Business Verification, advanced permission approval, and Marketing API Full access before it can serve live advertisers. Build a read-only `ads_read` integration first; add `ads_management` only for explicit campaign-management workflows. The normal production path is gated by review and verification, while the development-only Limited tier is materially easier but cannot support live advertisers.
verdict.activeEffort: 1–3 days, mostly implementing a reviewable OAuth flow, collecting compliance materials, recording permission demonstrations, and preparing reviewer access.
verdict.waitTime: A few days for Business Verification and up to several weeks for the overall review process (official); approximately 20 days is community-reported.
verdict.mainGate: Business Verification, App Review approval for advanced `ads_read` and/or `ads_management`, and qualification for Marketing API Full access.

recommendation.text: Create a Business app and use Facebook Login OAuth for each customer to authorize only the ad-account permissions the agent needs. Start with advanced `ads_read` for reporting, use explicit human-confirmed workflows before adding write access, and pursue Marketing API Full access for live advertiser workloads.

essentials.text: Default user tokens expire in hours. Exchange a valid short-lived token for a long-lived token that generally lasts about 60 days; Meta documents token exchange rather than a conventional refresh-token grant, and an expired token cannot be exchanged. Plan reconnection handling because data access expires after 90 days of user inactivity and requires reauthorization.

steps.title: Add products and configure app settings

detail.text: In App Dashboard, add Facebook Login and Marketing API, connect the app to the operating Business, and configure the app icon, public privacy-policy URL, category, business email, and supported platform details required for review.

steps.title: Prepare redirect-URI checklist

detail.text: Use this checklist while entering Valid OAuth Redirect URIs in Facebook Login settings so the authorization and token-exchange callback URI remains exact and tenant-safe.

sources.quote: `redirect_uri`. This argument is required and must be the same as the original `request_uri` that you used when starting the OAuth login process.

`state`. A string value created by your app to maintain
state between the request and callback.

steps.output:
Redirect URI checklist:
1. Register only fixed HTTPS callbacks, e.g. https://app.example.com/oauth/meta/callback.
2. Use that exact string in the authorize request and token exchange.
3. Never construct a redirect URI from tenant, account, or request input.
4. Store a signed, short-lived state value server-side.
5. Reject callback requests with missing, expired, or mismatched state.
6. Keep staging and production callback URLs separately registered.

steps.title: Implement authorization-code login and token storage

detail.text: Implement server-side OAuth code exchange using `response_type=code`, a validated state value, the exact registered redirect URI, and the app secret; encrypt and tenant-bind the resulting token rather than exposing the secret or token exchange to the browser.

sources.quote: When `code` is received, it has to be [exchanged for an access token using an endpoint](#exchangecode). The call will need to be server-to-server
